observation_summary:
FastMath.pow returns a positive result instead of a negative result when raising a negative base to an odd integer exponent in the range
 [2^52, 2^53).
reasoning_summary: The bug occurs because the implementation of FastMath.pow incorrectly assumes that any double-precision floating-point number with an absolute value greater than or equal to 2^52 is an even integer. In IEEE 754 double-precision format, integers are represented exactly only up to 2^53. Between 2^52 and 2^53, odd integers can still be represented. By using 2^52 as the threshold for assuming an exponent is an even integer, the code incorrectly treats certain odd integers as even, leading to an incorrect sign for negative bases. The fix correctly updates the threshold to 2^53, which is the point beyond which all representable floating-point numbers are indeed even integers.
